title: Compound sentences, くれる, あげる and the て-form
summary: The て-form links clauses into one long sentence with a single tense at the end, and くれる / あげる describe giving and doing something for someone.

blocks.text: Until now each sentence has been a single train. Real Japanese chains them. This lesson shows how, with a little story: a cat sits by a river while her big sister reads and ignores her. The cat is the heroine of lessons 11 to 14.
A **position noun** like そば (beside) or 上 (top) works like any noun, so the place takes **に**: 川のそばにいる.

blocks.jp: ある日、猫は川のそばにいた。
blocks.en: One day the cat was beside the river.

blocks.text: **ある** ("to exist") also shows lesson 6 at work. The engine ある is turned into a white engine in front of a noun, so ある日 is "a certain day" ("one day") and ある本 is "a certain book".
本がある → ある本: the engine becomes a white engine.

A verb in **て-form** that is not the last word says: this clause is finished, and **more is coming**. Tense is marked **only once, at the very end**, and it covers the whole sentence. So 読んでいて on its own could be "is reading" or "was reading" until the final past marker settles it.
Two clauses, one tense at the end.

blocks.title: Where the tense shows
rows: Yes: past, for the whole sentence

blocks.jp: 姉は本を読んでいて、猫と話さなかった。
blocks.en: My sister was reading a book and did not talk with the cat.

blocks.text: くれる and あげる: giving

Both mean "give", and the difference is direction. In Japanese you always place yourself **below** other people. **くれる** is giving **down to me or my group**; **あげる** is giving **up and out to someone else**.
友達が私に本をくれた。 The gift travels down to me.

blocks.jp: 友達が私に本をくれた。
blocks.en: A friend gave me a book.

blocks.jp: 私は友達にプレゼントをあげた。
blocks.en: I gave my friend a present.

blocks.text: Put either after a **て-form verb** and it means doing the action **for someone's benefit**: 〜てくれる (someone does it for me), 〜てあげる (I do it for someone).

blocks.jp: 友達が宿題を手伝ってくれた。
blocks.en: A friend helped me with my homework.

blocks.jp: 弟に宿題を手伝ってあげた。
blocks.en: I helped my little brother with his homework.

blocks.text: Now the story sentence has every piece: a て-form clause, くれる after a て-form, and the tense only at the end.

blocks.jp: 姉は本を読んでいて、遊んでくれなかった。
blocks.en: My sister was reading a book and did not play with me.

blocks.title: Remember
items: **て-form** = "this clause is done, more follows". The **tense is marked once**, at the end.
**くれる**: giving **to me / my group**. **あげる**: giving **to someone else**.
**〜てくれる / 〜てあげる**: doing something **for** someone.
**ある日** = "one day"; position nouns take **に** (**川のそばに**).

questions.note: に marks who receives.
に marks the receiver.
